Stated Claim / Post Context:
Plane passenger ignites heated debate over window seat etiquette after clash with crying child: 'I will not be the bigger person'

Sharna Kite recently took to TikTok to share her vexing encounter with a fellow traveler. And the video, which has been viewed more than 7.4 million times, sparked a firestorm in the comments.

Actual Article Body:
By RAVEN SAUNT, US LIFESTYLE EDITOR

Updated:  07:02 AEDT, 14 October 2026

A plane passenger has sparked a fierce debate about window seat etiquette after clashing with a crying child onboard.

Sharna Kite recently took to TikTok to share her vexing encounter with a fellow traveler.

In the clip, Kite, who was sitting directly next to the window, keeps the camera steady as she swiftly raises the blind.

But just seconds later, the hand of a toddler in the row in front reaches behind him to pull it back down.

The tot can be heard crying and whimpering in the background as Kite once again raises the shade.

The young boy continues to grumble as he and Kite become locked in battle as each repeatedly reaches for it in turn.

Eventually, Kite appears to hold the blind up in place and, with the boy unable to out-muscle her, he lets out a disgruntled squeal.

Kite added overlaid text that read: 'Unfortunately no, I will not be the bigger person.'

A plane passenger has sparked a fierce debate about window seat etiquette after clashing with a crying child onboard (stock image)

The video, which has so far been viewed more than 7.4 million times, sparked a firestorm in the comments.

On the one hand, there were some who thought Kite was in the wrong for not allowing the kid to get his own way.

'Everyone saying kids are so annoying but have we thought about how the kid might be annoyed too?' one wrote.

'I just realized nearly everyone doesn't treat kids as beings, this is disgusting,' another added.

'No because if you don't want the light buy a sleep mask or drape something over your eyes. If I have a window seat I want to look out of my window,' a third said.

But, on the other hand, many agreed that Kite should get to dictate how the blind sits since it is predominantly serving her aisle.

'If you have to reach back then it's not your window,' one simply shared.

'Where on earth are the kid's parents? As a parent I would NEVER let my kid do that! They have to respect others and learn the concept of no too!' another added.

There is no official protocol on window shades on planes but the unwritten rule is that the person sitting in the window seat controls the shade (stock image)

'When I was a kid, I was terrified of upsetting strangers.

'The audacity children have is genuinely insane,' another shared.

There is no official protocol on window shades on planes but the unwritten rule is that the person sitting in the window seat controls the shade during normal cruising flight.

Flight attendants have ultimate authority and can require shades to be open or closed for safety and cabin comfort.
